### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **16** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**15** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx`  _(via OBJECT_NOT_FOUND (literal, a string literal in a comment on a changed line; a string literal in historyCounterVerdict; a string literal in objectNotFoundError; a string literal in resolveSoleOrganizationId))_

> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 71 pages)`
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **149** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 901e7cf13abd61afb4990ebc1e3b9cd36cf9b33d` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c84a16078041482977cd8ac13a1e738ec366f917` — the merge of head `2df18ea792202e43ae85a0d3a7d4a5ff683af9b7` into base `901e7cf13abd61afb4990ebc1e3b9cd36cf9b33d`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c84a16078041482977cd8ac13a1e738ec366f917 && git checkout c84a16078041482977cd8ac13a1e738ec366f917
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 901e7cf13abd61afb4990ebc1e3b9cd36cf9b33d 2df18ea792202e43ae85a0d3a7d4a5ff683af9b7 && git checkout -B drift-repro 901e7cf13abd61afb4990ebc1e3b9cd36cf9b33d && git merge --no-ff 2df18ea792202e43ae85a0d3a7d4a5ff683af9b7

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 901e7cf13abd61afb4990ebc1e3b9cd36cf9b33d
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 901e7cf13abd61afb4990ebc1e3b9cd36cf9b33d` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `6752a29827847c463c90f5171d0ee9f7b083e5d8`
Local-runs: none

**What was read:**
- Card #21516: the body and all six comments. These are triage 5964437602, claim 5964938685 (revision 2), os-dev report 5965771442, seat answer 5965797270, the `domain:cli` pointer 5967297021, and the ACCEPT and handover 5968082941. At this read (12:21Z), 5965771442 was the only os-dev report on the card.
- PR #21545: the body, and the 80-file net diff (+1065 / −212) against merge base `1ca1eb0972`.
- The check-runs on the head.
- Repo text at the head, for the precedents and the policy cited below.

**Check-runs at this read:**
- 46 runs across 35 check names. None is `in_progress`.
- Latest run of each check: 30 are `success` and 5 are `skipped`. The skips are Auto Label, Build Docs, Check PR Size, Console Pin Gate and Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in).
- `Part-of PR must not also close its card`: the 08:44Z `failure` is superseded by the 09:18Z `success`, which ran after the body patch.
- All green: Test Core 1–6, Dogfood Regression Gate 1–3, Temporal Conformance, the four Type Check jobs, Lint & Repo Gates (which runs the ADR-0087 registration and empty-changeset gates) and Check Changeset (10:06Z).

### ① Derived judgments

**1. New `@objectstack/core` export `objectNotFoundError(object)`: RIGHT.**
- **The envelope:**
  - `code: 'OBJECT_NOT_FOUND'`, `status: 404`, `object` holding the name as passed, and the message `Object '…' not found`.
  - These are the same three properties, in the same order, with the same message template as the inline literal the door's `assertObjectRegistered` used to throw.
  - Its shape is `recordNotFoundError`'s: code, status and object set on a plain `Error`.
- **The home:**
  - ADR-0076 D2 says `@objectstack/objectql` "does **not** import `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`", and `core-boundary.ratchet.test.ts` enforces it. So `engine.ts` cannot import the door's module.
  - `core` is the lowest package both callers already depend on. That is `recordNotFoundError`'s #7867 move, step for step.
  - The factory has two callers, the door gate and the engine resolver, and there is no second definition in the tree.
- **Additive:** one `export *` line on core's `.` entry.
  - Nothing that existed is renamed, removed or retyped, and `metadata-protocol`'s index is untouched.
  - ADR-0076 D8 (no governance in the engine) is not crossed: the refusal reads only the engine's own registry.
- **Tests:** core has no unit test of the factory. The envelope is pinned through its consumers, whose cases assert `code`, `status` and `object`. The precedent has no core unit test either. Not blocking.

**2. The accept-set narrowing of the engine's in-process verbs: RIGHT, per triage 5964437602's ruling.**
- **The eight verbs:**
  - `find`, `findOne`, `count`, `aggregate`, `insert`, `update`, `delete` and `validate`.
  - Each makes `resolveObjectName` its first statement. At the head these are engine.ts :11831, :12131, :17054, :17166, :12775, :13827, :16520 and :12475.
  - `insertMany` delegates to `insert` after an array check only.
  - `resolveObjectName` now throws `objectNotFoundError(name)` where it used to return `StorageNameMapping.resolveTableName({ name })`.
- **Before any hook, middleware or driver:** yes. In every verb the throw precedes alias folding, `assertWriteAllowed`, hooks, middleware and `getDriver`.
  - No verb re-enters another verb with the resolved table name, so the change does not depend on a second resolution of an already-resolved name.
- **One name space, exactly:**
  - The registry resolves only registered names: `computeFQN` returns the short name, and the FQN fallback is that same key. So no alias of a registered name escapes.
  - A re-spelling the driver would have mapped onto a protected table is now refused.
- **Callers already guarded:** `referenceExists`, `planCascadeAtomicity` and `cascadeDeleteRelations` already wrap the resolver in try/catch. They are unchanged.
- **`judgeFilter`:** unchanged for every registered name, and for every unregistered name without `__`.
  - One byte drift: for an unregistered legacy-FQN spelling (`ns__short`), the verdict's object string is now the spelling as given. It used to be the suffix that `resolveTableName`'s legacy strip produced.
  - That is truthful and not a contract change, and the spec docblock matches it.
- **The org probe asks the registry first:**
  - When `sys_organization` is unregistered, `probeInstallOrganizations` returns and memoises `[]`.
  - That is the memoised answer the old fall-through gave, on a tolerant driver (`[]`) and on a strict one (a missing table) alike.
  - The catch arm is unchanged (`isMissingTableError` only).
  - Pinned in `engine-organization-probe-outage.test.ts`: the driver stub throws if it is asked, zero `sys_organization` reads happen, and the write proceeds unstamped.
- **The driver path left for host code:**
  - `getDriverForObject`, `datasource` and raw `execute` are members of the engine.
  - A body's `ScopedContext` holds the engine privately and exposes only `object()`, `sudo()`, `withRunAs()` and `transaction()`.
  - The dogfood premise and the new pin reach the driver as host code.

**3. `OBJECT_NOT_FOUND` byte identity at the data door: RIGHT.**
- `assertObjectRegistered` only swaps its inline literal for the factory: the same message template and the same three properties.
- The wire answer comes from `mapDataError`'s `OBJECT_NOT_FOUND` arm (`types/data-error-classification.ts`). It reads `code` and `object` and ships its own fixed sentence.
- So the HTTP shape a client sees is unchanged: 404, `code`, `object` and that sentence.
- The new pin's reference case asserts the door's 404 `OBJECT_NOT_FOUND`, with no table content in the answer.

**4. The `metadata-protocol` readers' absence rule: RIGHT, and narrow.**
- **seed-loader `resolveSoleOrganizationId`:**
  - The read counts as absence only when `isMissingTableError(error, 'sys_organization')` holds, or when `code === 'OBJECT_NOT_FOUND'` and `object === 'sys_organization'`.
  - Everything else is rethrown, so #12852 holds.
- **`SysMetadataRepository.historyCounterVerdict`:**
  - It returns 1 only on a missing table for `this.historyTable`, or on `OBJECT_NOT_FOUND` with `object === this.historyTable`.
  - Otherwise its one-time error report and the rethrow are unchanged.
  - A 1 for an unregistered history object cannot collide: the same engine rule refuses the append into that object.
- Neither reader keys on message text, on `status` or on the bare code. A refusal attributed to another object propagates, and so does every driver fault. Neither reader swallows a broader class.

**5. The test migration (69 test files): RIGHT.**
- **What the diff scan finds:**
  - No `.skip`, `.todo`, `.only`, `it.fails` or `skipIf` is added or removed.
  - 41 `expect(` lines are removed and 48 added.
  - Each removed line is replaced by one of three things: an assertion of the refusal (`code` and `status`, plus zero `writes` or `seen` where the test watched a driver), a stricter witness, or the reshaped noise reading below.
  - No matcher is loosened. For example, `resolves.toEqual([])` becomes `rejects.toMatchObject({ code, status })`, and `writes` `toHaveLength(1)` becomes `toHaveLength(0)`.
- **#3770 case B (`protocol-unregistered-object.test.ts`):**
  - The door's `findData` 404 assertion is unchanged.
  - The storage witness now reads the stub store directly, so the case still fails for the right reason.
  - The engine assertion flips from "serves the row" to `rejects.toMatchObject(OBJECT_NOT_FOUND)`, and header item ② gains one sentence.
  - The flip is right. #3770's ruling is the door gate, which stands. Its "the engine does not reject" line described the mechanism of the time, as the seat said.
- **#7929-ruled pins: none touched.**
  - No changed file references #7929 or `captureExpectedCrossFieldRefusalNoise`, or touches the cross-field withholding pins (`cross-field-refusal-operand-withhold.test.ts` and the driver-sql cross-field suites).
  - The pins that do change their reading are the table-keyed `captureExpectedReadRefusals` noise pins (commit 13a6cb4ad's family): 17 runtime files plus `trigger-record-change` go from `silentChannels()` to `tablesSeen()` equal to empty.
  - Each keeps its subject on the new mechanism, and a regression that sends the probe back to the driver turns it red. ③ R3 covers the PR body's mislabel of this family.
- **Deletions by design:**
  - `engine-20822` folds its five verb-path type-blind-lowering cases into one refusal case. A verb can no longer reach that branch for an unregistered name.
  - The typed control and the judge case stay.
  - ADR-0053 D-D1 item 7 ("A seam that cannot applies the rewrite type-blind") stays true and is not edited.
  - The #21242 "compared as written" registry-less cases in `engine-aggregate-filter` and `-having-comparand-shape` move to two places, both present at the head: the direct `applyInMemoryAggregation` case (filter :950) and the registered cases (having :964).
- **Fixtures that now register an object still test what their titles claim:**
  - The stored-metadata family is registered "as a boot does" in the objectql metadata-write harnesses and the 14 rest harnesses. It is registered after the DDL, so an unprovisioned store still answers with a missing table. rest-unknown-object-heuristic's [#5462] fault leg still reaches its failing driver.
  - The authz read set is registered after DDL or boot in four plugin-security files and in http-conformance. The missing-table "no grants" answer is preserved.
  - approvals registers the delegation and organization objects, unprovisioned. service-settings registers `sys_secret` and `sys_setting_audit`.
  - channel-asymmetry registers its probe object after boot, so it still measures the real two-channel refusal.
  - `engine-summary-recompute-context` registers its probe object, so the refusal stays the permission gate's. Without it the test would pin the wrong refusal.
  - The cli served-boot control witnesses each hook read by its recorded `OBJECT_NOT_FOUND` answer, and adds an assertion that no driver line is printed.

**6. Triage 5964437602's three pins: MET.**
- **The measured exit:** the new `packages/runtime/src/unresolved-object-name.actions-door.pin.test.ts` boots bootStack's plugin set.
  - An action body run through REST `/actions` reads an out-of-band table that no registry names.
  - For both the administrator and the member, it answers 404 `OBJECT_NOT_FOUND`, and the sentinel value appears nowhere in the answer.
- **The control:** the same body shape on the registered `pin_note` answers 200 with the control row, for both roles.
- **#21454's seam pins:** `stored-metadata-reader-contexts.pin.test.ts`, `stored-metadata-reader-seam.test.ts` and the seam source are not in the diff, and Test Core is green on the head.
- The pin names no protected table, keeping to classes only. Its mechanism is the same unregistered-name path.

**7. `domain:cli` pointer 5967297021: SUPPORTED.**
- `insert`, `update` and `delete` refuse an unresolved name in their first statement, before hooks and middleware. A body's write under a re-spelled name never reaches a table.
- So PR #21563's seam, which keys on the passed name, needs no name normalisation.
- The diff touches no runtime seam file.

**8. Implied, but named by no changeset: untouched internal readers.**
- Two readers that this diff does not touch now see the refusal in compositions that do not register an object they read. They are ③ R1 and R2.
- Both fail loud, and no shipped boot path reaches either.
- Judged acceptable for this landing under triage's "refuse" ruling, and named for follow-up.

### ② Semver level

- **`@objectstack/core` minor, `Clause-②: yes`: RIGHT.**
  - An additive export on the `.` entry of a published package widens its public surface.
  - AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3 says "`yes` takes at least **`minor`**".
  - check-changeset-no-major says "a purely additive widening of a published package's public surface takes at least `minor`".
  - Every sentence of the body checks out against the factory.
- **`@objectstack/objectql` minor, BREAKING banner, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`: RIGHT.**
  - **BREAKING:** AGENTS.md says "`(narrowing)` is BREAKING".
  - **Why minor is allowed:**
    - The repo's launch-window convention, written in the guard that enforces it, `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`: "During the launch window we ship breaking changes as `minor`". Its end condition is GA (#14043).
    - The convention is still in force on main: there is no `.changeset/pre.json`, and the guard is green on this head.
    - During the window, the BREAKING banner and the ADR-0087 disposition are the mandatory carriers. Both are present, and `check:adr-0087-registration` is green.
  - **Why `no`:** this package's own published surface gains no export.
  - **The ADR-0087 disposition is right:**
    - No authorable key, export or shape is removed, so there is nothing for `migrate meta` to rewrite.
    - The before and after are stated, with the one-line fix: register the object; host code addresses the driver.
  - Every sentence checks out against the diff: the eight verbs plus `insertMany` via `insert`, the refusal before any hook, middleware or driver, `judgeFilter`, the org probe and the driver path.
- **`@objectstack/metadata-protocol` patch, `Clause-②: no`: RIGHT.**
  - The door's envelope is byte-identical.
  - The two readers' wider tolerance is internal.
  - There is no export, and no accept-set change of the package's own.
- **`@objectstack/spec` patch, `Clause-②: no`: RIGHT.**
  - The change is to the comment of the `IObjectQLEngine.judgeFilter` docblock only. It ships in `dist/*.d.ts`, so it publishes and needs a changeset.
  - It is not an accept-set change. The contract-review rule says 「从入口类型图不可达、且 `exports` 不可寻址的 `.d.ts` 是出货字节,⛔ 不是已发布接受集,改它不触发 `Clause-②: yes`」, and that holds all the more for a comment.
  - The docblock is true against `engine.ts`.
- **PR body `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`: CONSISTENT.**
  - `yes` comes from core's widening, and `(narrowing)` from objectql's BREAKING arm.
  - The level axis is satisfied: two packages are at minor.
  - The claim's original `no (narrowing)` was rightly replaced by the seat's correction 1.

### ③ Boundary flags

**Dev flags and report findings:**
- **The report's open question Q1 (completion scope A, B or C):** the seat answered A, and the head carries A in full. Closed.
  - objectql and runtime are migrated.
  - cli, services, plugins, rest, qa and triggers are measured, and triaged in the PR body.
  - No ADR text is edited: no `docs/adr` path is in the diff.
  - No #7929 pin changed.
- **The report's "NAMED-GAP RED", "Gates NOT fully reconciled" and "No ablation commit-revert run":** superseded. Every check is green on this head, and the PR body records a mutation leg and a restore leg (not re-run here, per the read-only shape). Closed.
- **The report's "scope beyond objectql/metadata-protocol/runtime is unmeasured":** measured on the branch per the PR body, and covered by Test Core 1–6 on the head. Closed.
- **The report's recorded decisions #3770, ADR-0053 and #12852:** answered by the seat, and verified in ① 5 and ① 4. Closed.
- **Out-of-scope finding 1 (metadata-write paths need the full stored-metadata family):** folded into this PR per the seat's answer. The harnesses register the family, and production registers it together. Closed; nothing to file.
- **Out-of-scope finding 2 (the noise reshape and the #3770 pin):** carried by this PR. Closed.
- **`domain:cli` pointer 5967297021:** answered in ① 7.
- **The seat's ACCEPT 5968082941:** tested, and its claims hold. Its census, though, is incomplete by R1 and R2. Its count of 36 successes matches the run count at its own read; the extra Check Changeset run came at 10:06Z.

**Reviewer findings:**
- **R1. Escalate as a follow-up card for `domain:engine`; not blocking.**
  - **The reader:** `LifecycleService.loadGovernance`'s tenant scan in `packages/objectql/src/lifecycle/lifecycle-service.ts` reads `sys_organization` best-effort. It treats only `isMissingTableError` as benign ("no `sys_organization` at all (a single-tenant kernel)").
  - **What changes:**
    - Take a composition with a settings service and lifecycle-declared objects but no `sys_organization` registered. That is the very lean shape this PR's seed-loader and engine-probe comments name.
    - There the engine's refusal now propagates, and every sweep aborts before applying any policy.
  - **Why it does not block:**
    - The direction is safe: nothing is reaped on incomplete evidence.
    - No shipped boot path reaches it: `os serve` auto-registers PlatformObjectsPlugin, and the census saw 0 fall-through events across four example apps.
  - **The gap and the fix:**
    - The census table's "every in-repo caller" leaves this reader out.
    - Fix shape: the registry-first guard that the engine probe and `MigrationRecoveryPlugin` already use.
    - The stale header of `packages/runtime/src/expected-read-refusal-noise.ts`, which still says the probe catches only a missing table, can ride along.
